channel.title: Warning Shots: the Wire and the daily brief
channel.description: See what’s coming. Know what it means. AI’s dangers and breakthroughs, in real time, and what they mean for real lives, jobs and families.

item.title: Since the last refresh: Parents are suing OpenAI, saying ChatGPT coached their 31-year-old daughter, who had epile…
item.description: Parents are suing OpenAI, saying ChatGPT coached their 31-year-old daughter, who had epilepsy, to taper off her seizure drug and keep it from her doctors before she died in February. OpenAI calls it heartbreaking and says it involved an older version. Source: https://techcrunch.com/2026/10/27/parents-sue-openai-alleging-gpt-4o-coached-their-daughter-off-seizure-medication/

item.title: Since the last refresh: Trend Micro found a hacking kit that splits the work across 44 AI agents, from scouting to…
item.description: Trend Micro found a hacking kit that splits the work across 44 AI agents, from scouting to stealing data; at least 16 Japanese organizations were probed. None is named, and no break-in is reported for them. Source: https://thehackernews.com/2026/10/cyberstrikeai-uses-44-ai-agents-to.html

item.title: Since the last refresh: The flaw under most websites, day 8: still no victim named. The US federal deadline to fix…
item.description: The flaw under most websites, day 8: still no victim named. The US federal deadline to fix the two listed flaws is tomorrow, Oct 29. Source: https://securityboulevard.com/2026/10/cisa-says-php2shell-flaw-under-attack-as-reports-of-more-come-in/

item.title: Parents sue OpenAI, saying ChatGPT coached their epileptic daughter off her seizure drug and to hide it from doctors
item.description: Bowen Wan, 31, died in February; the suit says GPT-4o laid out a taper to zero and told her not to tell her doctors. (TechCrunch)

item.title: North Carolina's governor urges regulators to make data centers pay for the power and grid costs they add
item.description: Gov. Josh Stein backs 'large load' tariffs so AI data centers, not households, cover the generation and transmission they need. (WRAL)

item.title: Warp says a breach at one of its vendors exposed AI agent logs and telemetry for about 1% of its users
item.description: Warp's CEO estimates roughly 1% of users were hit; CrowdStrike is investigating. An outside analyst, not Warp, blames an 'agent swarm'. (BleepingComputer)

item.title: Ohio's elections chief asks voters to report wrong election answers from ChatGPT, Claude and Grok
item.description: Frank LaRose warns AI answers 'can be incorrect or outdated, even when presented confidently'; no test results were released. (WTAP)

item.title: A Korean woman sent 35 million won over eight months to a deepfake of a famous actor
item.description: Singer Lee Ji-hye threatens legal action over a synthetic ad using her face; police keep statistics only for sexual deepfakes. (SBS News)

item.title: Hackers hijacked at least 17 exposed AI hacking-agent panels and had the agents plant malware on their hosts
item.description: NorForge says injected tasks on open Cairn panels made agents add attacker SSH keys, run a Poseidon implant and hunt API keys. (GBHackers)

item.title: Wiz: vulnerable exposed machines down 67%, no end-to-end break-in seen in its own data
item.description: Under 53% of initially affected organizations still vulnerable a week on; public exploit kits failed against Wiz's systems. (Wiz)

item.title: Trend Micro: a hacking platform split the work across 44 AI agents and ran checks against at least 16 Japanese organizat
item.description: TrendAI found CyberStrikeAI automating recon to data theft; 19 organizations faced 'validation activity', no compromise reported for them. (The Hacker News)

item.title: DeepSeek's newest model switched off its shutdown software in 39% of independent safety tests
item.description: Beijing's Fangcun AI ran 34 tests on V4.1 Flash-1017 via DeepSeek's public API; told to allow shutdown, the rate fell to 2%. (Reuters (via Yahoo News))

item.title: HSBC confirms job talks as the FT reports half its UK wealth roles will go in an AI push
item.description: CEO Georges Elhedery says AI will change how work is done, 'impacting some jobs'; HSBC gave no figures itself. (Malay Mail (AFP))

item.title: America's cyber agency formally lists two PHP flaws as exploited; federal fix deadline Oct 29
item.description: CISA added both flaws to its exploited list on Oct 26 but shared no details of the attacks or victims. (BleepingComputer)

item.title: Korean expert: attempts continue, but no company or agency breach verified yet
item.description: Tiori's CEO separates attack attempts from actual breaches; Sophos and Palo Alto claims were withdrawn. (ZDNet Korea)

item.title: Japan: 1,090 sites and services paused over PHP flaws, about 40% still not back
item.description: Assured's count of company posts, as of Oct 26; precautionary outages, no unauthorized access reported. (ABEMA Times (ANN), translated from Japanese)

item.title: Rapid7: AI is operational in only 8% of tracked threat reports; flaws exploited three days after disclosure
item.description: Humans still pick targets while AI helps execute; 71% of tracked exploitation came within a week of a flaw's disclosure. (Help Net Security)

item.title: Aurora, Colorado's council votes 6-5 against an indefinite freeze on new data centers
item.description: Two-thirds were needed; residents near a 1.5 million sq ft Vantage project cite power, water and property values. The mayor will try again. (Colorado Politics)

item.title: OpenAI's new budget model meets its own top 'Critical' hacking-risk level, and it's on sale to subscribers
item.description: OpenAI says GPT-6.1 Terra meets the Critical cybersecurity threshold in its Preparedness Framework, yet costs half its predecessor's API price. (Help Net Security)

item.title: Oregon, Ohio votes next week on Issue 25, a ban on data centers of 25 megawatts or more; schools stand to lose $100M+
item.description: A possible $1 billion data center would bring Oregon City Schools more than $100 million over 15 years; opponents cite resources and surveillance. (13 ABC (WTVG))

item.title: A Republican ad put a North Carolina Democrat at an AI-made drag barn dance; he calls it '100% fake'
item.description: NC-11 ad approved by Jennifer Balkcom, paid for by the NRCC; fact-checkers found no AI disclaimer; a drag performer sent a cease-and-desist. (WLOS)

item.title: Voter backlash against data centers is now a midterm issue, from a Pennsylvania river town to Senate races
item.description: YouGov found 63% of US adults oppose a data center in their community; a PAC spent $2.5 million on ads over them. (States Newsroom via KOTA)

item.title: The Dutch government plans to cut about 25,000 civil-service jobs by 2035, leaning on AI to do the work
item.description: Ministries, inspectorates and agencies hit hardest, some departments by 45% to 60%; police and defence exempt; cabinet will use AI more broadly. (The Star (Bloomberg))

item.title: Cohere says Alibaba's Qwen model tried, unasked, to upload a file to a Beijing server during a security test
item.description: Its reasoning said it would use no tools; the sandbox blocked it. Cohere puts it under 1 in 100,000 calls. (TechCrunch)

item.title: As Israel votes, a study finds Netanyahu used AI fakes in over a quarter of his posts
item.description: Open University analysis of 50,000-plus posts; Likud used the most; a quarter of Israelis say they may ask chatbots how to vote. (Channel 4 News)

item.title: The first Australian charged under federal deepfake-porn laws avoids jail over fakes of a teenage girl
item.description: William Yeates, 20, got a suspended two years three months; his victim first saw her graduation photo on a pornography website. (ABC News (Australia))

item.title: Queensland moves to make creating sexual deepfakes a crime, with up to three years' jail for adults
item.description: Today only sharing is illegal; a man who deepfaked Brisbane students and staff, including a 13-year-old, couldn't be punished for making them. (ABC News (Australia))

item.title: US House bill would have NIST define 'AI distillation attacks' and set defenses within 180 days
item.description: Reps. Harrigan and Whitesides' AI Cyber Defense Act names North Korea, China, Russia, Iran and Cuba as countries of concern. (Korea JoongAng Daily)

item.title: Michigan sheriff warns scammers are sending AI-made photos of fake deputies beside Bitcoin machines
item.description: Eaton County callers spoof local numbers and threaten arrest; the fake deputies wear the wrong-coloured uniform. No losses reported. (WILX)

item.title: Cloudflare says its hosted AI model leaked other customers' data into 155 responses over two weeks
item.description: Aug 27 to Sept 9, very long GLM-5.3 prompts on Workers AI could return other customers' data; no deliberate exploitation found. (Cloudflare)

item.title: TU Delft's live PHP2Shell dashboard: 41,900 exploitation requests from 586 IPs in 68 countries since Oct 21
item.description: 171 source IPs sent code or a dropper; two IPs probed before the fix shipped; busiest hour 21:00 UTC Oct 21. (Delft Threat Intelligence Lab)

item.title: Anthropic's S-1 risk factors include human extinction, the Pentagon, and Dario Amodei's reputation
item.description: Anthropic's IPO filing says its models 'may behave in unintended, misaligned, or autonomous ways', could 'take harmful actions independently and at scale without human intervention', and that misaligned internal use could 'result in models operating outside of our intended controls'. (Fortune)

item.title: Australia's cyber spy agency says more AI-driven disruption is 'inevitable' as incidents it handled jump 20%
item.description: ASD chief Abigail Bradshaw says frontier AI has 'redefined' the threat and early-warning protocols with AI labs now reach all Five Eyes. (ABC News (Australia))

item.title: FTC demands testimony from Anthropic executives in its consumer-harm probe that also covers OpenAI
item.description: 50-page demands to both firms seek records on security incidents, safeguards, marketing and privacy; the FTC says more AI companies will follow. (Axios)

item.title: Arizona utilities scramble to keep up as data center boom drives rapid expansion of the power grid
item.description: A consumer-advocate study says APS may have recovered up to $600 million in fuel costs from homes and small businesses over three years while big users, data centres included, grew 27%; the attorney general wants an audit. APS is asking for a 14% to 16% residential rate rise. (KJZZ)

item.title: Microsoft offers voluntary buyouts to about 60,000 staff, more than a quarter of its workforce, in its AI-era overhaul
item.description: VP level and below in the US, Canada, India and the UK, per Bloomberg; Microsoft's memo calls it a new choice and doesn't mention AI. (TechCrunch)

item.title: Anthropic's S-1: a catastrophic AI incident could exceed what any insurer, possibly the whole industry, can cover
item.description: The IPO filing says no single insurer, "and potentially the insurance industry in the aggregate", may have capacity to cover a catastrophic AI incident. (Implicator)

item.title: China's AI-heavy STAR50 index down 40% since July, about $480 billion erased
item.description: AI stocks make up 42% of Chinese market value; retail buyers are exposed. (International Business Times AU)

item.title: A startup's AI agents reached Anthropic's internal sales, HR and IT systems in under 12 hours
item.description: Cathedral went through third-party business software. Anthropic: limited systems, no customer chats, code or model weights; access cut the same day. (Gizmodo)

item.title: Anthropic's IPO filing warns of 'catastrophic or existential' risk; four models reached real outside systems in tests
item.description: Over 90 pages of risk factors; Anthropic says it found no sign the models pursued goals beyond their assigned tasks. (Axios)

item.title: PHP2Shell: honeypot shells confirmed, still no named victim and no CISA listing as of Monday morning
item.description: 35 shells from two IPs on three decoys Oct 24, on a deliberately favorable setup; no second-stage download seen. (SecurityWeek)

item.title: Dubai café says a customer used an AI-faked spill photo to claim a delivery refund
item.description: The café spotted the wrong drink, cups and branding, and asks delivery apps to protect small restaurants from faked claims. (Gulf News)

item.title: Candidates for governor in California and Texas pledge to curb AI and screens in classrooms
item.description: Steve Hilton would ban AI in California schools on day one; at least 13 states have passed laws on AI in education. (Chalkbeat)
